definitions.plan: The Biking and Rolling Plan's high-quality test (printed p. 24; Appendix G, Toole Design connectivity memo of 2024-02-13): Class I, Class IV and Slow Streets; Class II with Bike Comfort Index above 80; Class III with traffic calming and BCI above 80. A direction row qualifies by its own class; a Class II or III row qualifies when its block's 2023 Draft BCI (bci) clears 80. BCI is one 2023 snapshot held fixed for every year. A Class III row also needs traffic calming on its block by that year, read from DataSF abhw-ffzx (mid-block) and bp3t-bd4t (intersection devices at either end of the block); class_iii_calm_street_no_calming_miles is what that condition removes.
definitions.strict: Class I, Class IV and Slow Street rows only, no BCI test. Written as all_ages_strict_miles; no page shows it.

all_ages.rule: A direction row is all-ages when it is CLASS I or CLASS IV, or CLASS II or CLASS III on a block whose BCI is above 80, or on an implemented Slow Street from its install year. A block is within reach of a point when any of its rows qualifies.

method.year_state: A block's class in year Y is its class in the nearest archived copy captured after the end of Y, unless UPDATE_YR says the change came after Y, in which case it is the class in the nearest earlier copy, or unknown when there is none. A block exists in Y when INSTALL_YR is Y or earlier, or blank. A block in the earlier copy and gone from the later one is counted through Y.
method.miles: Row miles, the plan's unit: every direction row's length, summed, so a two-way street with a lane each way counts twice. A live row is measured from its own line geometry (equirectangular projection about 37.76 N); an archived row on a block still in the layer at the live layer's mean row length for that block, since the archived exports keep no geometry for those; an archived row on a block since dropped from its own geometry. Slow Street blocks outside the bikeway layer count their length 2 times. Centreline miles, one length per block, are written beside every row-mile figure. Off-street paths with no CNN (Presidio trails, Golden Gate Park, Kirkham, SFSU and other paths) are keyed by their endpoints and counted; the Presidio's are also shown separately.
method.gap_fill: A block present in an earlier and a later capture but missing from one between is carried through the gap with its earlier record.
method.timing: Network state is the end of the year (or the latest capture for the current year); schools and libraries are counted as open on 09-01 of the year.
method.reach: Walking distance along OpenStreetMap's walk network (OSMnx's walk filter plus cycle paths; see site/data/bike-history/walk-reach.json for the copy read) from the census block's interior point, the school's CDE coordinate or the branch's City Facilities coordinate to the nearest all-ages line, at most 0.25 miles by default; the point joins the network at the nearest street or path in a straight line, and a line is reached where it passes within 20 m of a walkable way (scripts/walknet.py). reach_thresholds names the shorter distances the overview also offers. The lines reached include the pandemic Slow Street blocks SFMTA dropped in December 2022, from their corridor's install year through 2021, as the miles do (reach_without_dropped_slow_streets on each row gives the figures without them).
method.reach_thresholds: Four distances, the plan's quarter mile (402 m) by default, one and two city blocks (440 and 880 feet), and 1000 feet, about the 300 m walk to a protected bikeway the ITDP Atlas of Sustainable City Transport measures. The population-weighted average block, intersection to intersection on the street centerline over 240 tracts, is 416 feet (scripts/sf-block-length.py, https://data.sfgov.org/d/3psu-pn9h, read 2026-11-10), so one block is taken as 440 feet and two as 880, Bryan's figures; the measured typical block is 416 feet. Each row's reach_by_threshold carries the six reach figures at each.
method.population_denominator: Every block in San Francisco County, including Treasure Island and the Farallones.
method.school_denominator: K-12 schools: public schools of the counted types (see sources.schools) open on 09-01 of the year, by CDE OpenDate and ClosedDate, plus DataSF's active private elementary, high and K-12 schools from their open_date (a private school that closed earlier is missing). Charter schools are included (14 of the 221 open in 2026), as is the County Community school run in the county jail (1).
method.library_denominator: SFPL branches plus the Main Library in City Facilities, minus branches closed for renovation that year.

limits: Before 2021-03-25 no archived copy of the layer exists. Years 2015–2020 rest on INSTALL_YR alone: a block installed before 2021 and removed before the first capture is invisible, a block whose class was upgraded with no UPDATE_YR is credited with its later class in every year back to its install, and 23% of the live layer's miles carry no INSTALL_YR at all and are assumed present throughout. Treat network miles in those years as a floor.

All-ages miles before 2021 carry an uncertainty band of about ±32 miles in 2015, from two opposite errors. 54.5 miles have an unknown class in 2015 because UPDATE_YR is later and there is no earlier capture, and 31.5 of those are all-ages today, so the figure may be low by up to that much. In the other direction, 9.9 miles of CLASS IV are credited to 2015 by an INSTALL_YR of 2013 or earlier, before Caltrans defined Class IV (2014), so on those rows INSTALL_YR dates the street's first bikeway rather than the separated lane, and the figure may be high by up to that much. [inference — mine]

Between captures a change is dated by UPDATE_YR when the row carries one; otherwise it is credited to the year before the later capture. The 2022-12-09 to 2024-03-31 and 2024-03-31 to 2025-12-08 gaps are the widest.

Population for years other than 2020 is an ACS 5-year block-group estimate spread across blocks by census shares, so it is a five-year average, not a point count, and block-level shares are held at the nearest census. 2025 and 2026 are held at the 2020–2024 ACS, the latest released.

The Slow Streets dataset was last loaded 2024-01-18 and carries no removal dates; the pandemic-era Slow Streets that were dropped in 2022 are not in it, and 7 segments (the SoMa streets) carry no install date and are counted from 2022. The dropped corridors are traced from SFMTA's 2020 and 2021 Board reports (scripts/lib/slow_corridors.py) and counted in the all-ages miles and the reach from their install year through 2021: 213 blocks, 21.2 all-ages miles in 2021 that no other all-ages line covered, adding 4.2 points of residents within a quarter mile in 2020. The reports give each corridor's extent as approved; where a corridor went in shorter, these years are high by the difference.

The CDE directory is the 2025-10-05 archive capture, so schools opened or closed after that date are missing. School coordinates are CDE's; most schools closed before 2015 carry none, and the one school open in the window without one (Gateway to College, closed 2016) is left out.
Library closures are entered by hand from SFPL's pages; only the Mission Branch's renovation closure is recorded. The system-wide COVID closure of March 2020 to May 2021 is not treated as a closure.

The map lights a point in exactly the years it is within reach, so a point reached only through a dropped Slow Street or a removed bikeway goes grey when it went. In 2026, 246 blocks (35,369 residents at the 2020 count) and 3 branches that were within a quarter mile of an all-ages line in an earlier year are not.
